en: Sahetukaduka (The Dyad on States with Roots)
Dependent on a state with root-cause, a state without root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state with root-cause, a state without root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state with root-cause, states both without root-cause and not without root-cause arise by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a rootless state, a rootless state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a rootless state, a state that is not with-root arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a rootless state, states that are both not with-root and not rootless arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on both a state with root-cause and a state without root-cause, a state without root-cause arises by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on both a state with root-cause and a state without root-cause, a state without root-cause arises by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on both a state with root-cause and a state without root-cause, states that are neither with root-cause nor without root-cause arise by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition, there are nine; in the object condition, six; in the predominance condition, five …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, nine. (The "Conascent" chapter and the "Investigation" chapter should also be expanded in detail.)
